extracted.intended_audience: covered entities (health care providers, health programs/activities, recipients of federal funds), compliance officers, Section 1557 Coordinators, legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and operational standards that health-care covered entities must implement to comply with HHS Section 1557 nondiscrimination obligations, including policies, procedures, training, notices, accessibility, language access, and enforcement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of a Section 1557 Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must ensure that, at minimum, the Section 1557 Coordinator: (1) receives, reviews, and processes grievances filed under the grievance procedure; (2) coordinates the covered entity's recordkeeping requirements; (3) coordinates effective implementation of the covered entity's language access procedures; (4) coordinates effective implementation of the covered entity's effective communication procedures; (5) coordinates effective implementation of the covered entity's reasonable modification procedures; and (6) coordinates training of relevant employees, including maintaining documentation required by such section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator duties map to grievance processing, recordkeeping, language access, effective communication, reasonable modifications, and training/documentation (see §92.8(c)–(f), §92.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written policies and procedures — general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must implement written policies and procedures in its health programs and activities that are designed to comply with the requirements of this part. The policies and procedures must include an effective date and be reasonably designed, taking into account the size, complexity, and the type of health programs or activities undertaken by a covered entity, to ensure compliance with this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should be tailored to the entity's scale and activities and must be dated. They form the basis for training, grievance processes, language access, effective communication, and reasonable modification processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination policy content
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must implement a written policy that, at minimum, states the covered entity does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin (including LEP and primary language), sex (consistent with §92.101(a)(2)), age, or disability; that the covered entity provides language assistance services and appropriate auxiliary aids and services free of charge when necessary; that the covered entity will provide reasonable modifications for individuals with disabilities; and that provides the current contact information for the Section 1557 Coordinator (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR considers it a best practice to indicate in the nondiscrimination policy if the entity has been granted a temporary exemption or assurance of exemption under §92.302(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures (entities with ≥15 employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity that employs fifteen or more persons must implement written grievance procedures that provide for the prompt and equitable resolution of grievances alleging any action that would be prohibited by section 1557 or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities subject to this paragraph must retain grievance records alleging discrimination on listed bases for no less than three calendar years (include grievance, complainant contact info if provided, alleged discriminatory action and basis, filing/resolution dates, resolution, and other pertinent info). The entity must keep complainant identity confidential except as required by law or as necessary to carry out the purposes of the part (including investigations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access procedures — written requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must implement written language access procedures describing its process for providing language assistance services to individuals with limited English proficiency when required under §92.201.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum procedures must include coordinator contact information; how employees identify LEP individuals; how employees obtain the services of qualified interpreters and translators; names of qualified bilingual staff; and a list of electronic/written translated materials, their languages, issuance dates, and how to access electronic translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective communication procedures — written requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must implement written effective communication procedures describing the covered entity's process for ensuring effective communication for individuals with disabilities when required under §92.202.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum procedures must include coordinator contact information; how employees obtain services of qualified interpreters used to communicate with individuals with disabilities (including names of qualified interpreter staff); and how to access appropriate auxiliary aids and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modification procedures — written requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must implement written procedures describing its process for making reasonable modifications to its policies, practices, or procedures when necessary to avoid discrimination on the basis of disability as required under §92.205.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures must include coordinator contact information; a description of the process for responding to requests for changes/exceptions/adjustments; and a process for determining whether making the modification would fundamentally alter the nature of the program or activity, including identifying an alternative modification that does not result in a fundamental alteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to combine policies and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity may combine the content of Section 1557 policies and procedures with policies required under title VI, section 504, title IX, and the Age Act if section 1557 and its provisions are clearly addressed therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining is allowed so long as Section 1557 obligations are clearly and fully addressed in the combined documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes and review of policies and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must review and revise the policies and procedures required by paragraphs (b) through (g) as necessary to ensure they are current and in compliance; and may change a policy or procedure at any time, provided such changes comply with section 1557 and this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain up-to-date policies; material changes trigger training obligations for affected staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training of relevant employees
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must train relevant employees on the civil rights policies and procedures required by §92.8, as necessary and appropriate for employees to carry out their functions consistent with this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training timing: to each relevant employee as soon as possible but no later than 30 days following implementation of policies and no later than 300 days following July 5, 2024; thereafter to new relevant employees within a reasonable period after hiring; and to employees affected by a material change within a reasonable period after the change. 'Relevant employees' includes permanent and temporary staff who interact with patients/public; make decisions affecting patient care (including exec leadership and legal counsel); or perform tasks affecting patients' financial obligations (billing/collections). Entities must contemporaneously document completion of training and retain documentation for no less than three calendar years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of nondiscrimination — required content
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must provide a notice of nondiscrimination that includes: (i) statement the entity does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin (including LEP and primary language), sex, age, or disability; (ii) that the entity provides reasonable modifications and appropriate auxiliary aids and services (e.g., qualified interpreters, information in alternate formats) free of charge and timely when necessary; (iii) that the entity provides language assistance services including electronic and written translated documents and oral interpretation free of charge and timely; (iv) how to obtain the reasonable modifications/auxiliary aids/language assistance; (v) contact information for the Section 1557 Coordinator; (vi) availability of the grievance procedure and how to file a grievance; (vii) details on how to file a discrimination complaint with OCR; and (viii) how to access the covered entity's website with required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice wording must cover required elements and provide actionable contact/filing info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of nondiscrimination — distribution and display requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must be provided: (i) on an annual basis to participants, beneficiaries, enrollees (including late/special enrollees), and applicants; (ii) upon request; (iii) at a conspicuous location on the entity's website; and (iv) in clear and prominent physical locations, in no smaller than 20-point sans serif font, where it is reasonable to expect individuals seeking service to be able to read or hear the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities may combine this notice with notices required by other referenced regulations if the combined notice clearly informs individuals of their civil rights under Section 1557 and includes each required element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of availability of language assistance services — content and languages
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must provide a notice stating it provides language assistance services and appropriate auxiliary aids and services free of charge when necessary for compliance. The notice must be provided in English and at least the 15 languages most commonly spoken by LEP individuals in the State(s) where the entity operates, and in alternate formats for individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure translated notices in the 15 most common languages for the relevant geography and make available in accessible alternate formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of availability of language assistance — distribution channels
rubrics_metrics.description: The language assistance notice must be provided: (1) annually to participants/beneficiaries/enrollees/applicants; (2) upon request; (3) on the entity's website; (4) in clear and prominent physical locations in ≥20-point sans serif font; and (5) in specified electronic and written communications (including nondiscrimination notice, notice of privacy practices, application/intake forms, denial/termination notices, communications requiring response, public health emergency communications, consent forms, discharge papers, billing/collections materials and good faith estimates, complaint forms, patient/member handbooks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list of communication types indicates where notice must be included; ensure translations are embedded in these documents/communications when provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance deemed via opt-out or primary-language documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity shall be deemed in compliance with this section with respect to an individual if it either: (1) on an annual basis, provides the individual the option to opt out of receipt of the notice in their primary language and through appropriate auxiliary aids and services (with conditions protecting rights and documenting opt-out), or (2) documents the individual's primary language and either provides all materials and communications in that language or provides the notice in that language in all communications identified in paragraph (c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opt-out conditions: cannot condition receipt of aid on opting out; must inform the individual of right to receive notice on request; document opt-out annually; non-response is not treated as opt-out. Documentation approach requires providing materials in the documented primary language or tailored notice in those communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibition on discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in title I of the ACA, an individual must not, on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or any combination thereof, be excluded from participation in, be denied the benefits of, or otherwise be subjected to discrimination under any health program or activity operated by a covered entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the broad, overarching nondiscrimination mandate applicable across covered programs and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination on the basis of sex includes, but is not limited to, discrimination on the basis of sex characteristics (including intersex traits); pregnancy or related conditions; sexual orientation; gender identity; and sex stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities must interpret 'sex' broadly to include listed subcategories when applying nondiscrimination protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference to specific prohibitions under other civil-rights statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: In any health program or activity to which this part applies, a recipient and State Exchange must comply with specific prohibitions on discrimination in the Department's implementing regulations for title VI, section 504, title IX, and the Age Act, with specified term substitutions (e.g., 'recipient or State Exchange' in place of 'recipient'; 'individual' in place of 'student/employee/applicant').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where cross-referenced regs use narrower terms, those terms are to be mapped to 'individual' or 'recipient or State Exchange' as appropriate; the enumerated prohibitions do not limit the general prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful access for individuals with limited English proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must take reasonable steps to provide meaningful access to each individual with limited English proficiency (including companions with LEP) eligible to be served or likely to be directly affected by its health programs and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a fact-dependent evaluation of what 'reasonable steps' entail, considering nature/importance of the program and the particular communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language assistance services — quality and privacy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Language assistance services required must be provided free of charge, be accurate and timely, and protect the privacy and independent decision-making ability of the individual with LEP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy, timeliness, and confidentiality are core service quality metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified interpreter and translator requirement; machine translation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When interpretation services are required, a covered entity must offer a qualified interpreter. When translation services are required, a covered entity must utilize the services of a qualified translator. If machine translation is used for text that is critical to rights/benefits or where accuracy is essential or for complex/technical language, the translation must be reviewed by a qualified human translator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualified human professionals for interpretation/translation; machine translation may be used only with human review in high-stakes/complex contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of LEP compliance (Director's factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating whether a covered entity has met its obligation to provide meaningful access, the Director shall (1) evaluate and give substantial weight to the nature and importance of the health program or activity and the particular communication at issue, and (2) take into account other relevant factors, including the effectiveness of the covered entity's written language access procedures implemented pursuant to §92.8(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance assessment is context-sensitive and gives weight to program importance and written procedures' effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted use of certain persons to interpret or facilitate communication
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must not: (1) require an individual with LEP to provide/pay for their own interpreter; (2) rely on an adult not qualified as an interpreter except as a temporary emergency measure or where the LEP individual specifically requests the accompanying adult to interpret in private with a qualified interpreter present and documented; (3) rely on a minor child to interpret except as a temporary emergency measure; or (4) rely on staff other than qualified interpreters, qualified translators, or qualified bilingual/multilingual staff to communicate with LEP individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-qualified adults and minors are strictly limited to temporary emergency exceptions; accompanying-adult reliance requires explicit documented private request and presence/confirmation by a qualified interpreter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video remote interpreting (VRI) service standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If providing a qualified interpreter through video remote interpreting services, the covered entity must ensure the modality allows meaningful access and provide: (1) real-time, full-motion video and audio over a dedicated high-speed, wide-bandwidth connection that delivers high-quality images without lags/choppiness; (2) sharply delineated image large enough to display interpreter's and participant's faces; (3) clear, audible transmission of voices; and (4) adequate training to users so they can quickly set up and operate the VRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical quality and user training are required to ensure VRI provides meaningful access equivalent to in-person interpreting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio remote interpreting service standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If providing a qualified interpreter through audio remote interpreting services, the covered entity must ensure the modality allows meaningful access and provide: (1) real-time audio over a dedicated high-speed, wide-bandwidth connection delivering high-quality audio without lags; (2) clear, audible transmission; and (3) adequate training to users to set up and operate the services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audio-only remote interpreting requires equivalent emphasis on connectivity, audio clarity, and user training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of language assistance services not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require an individual with limited English proficiency to accept language assistance services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals may decline services, but the entity must still offer and make services available when needed; declines should be documented per other procedural requirements where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective communication obligations for individuals with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must take appropriate steps to ensure communications with individuals with disabilities (including companions) are as effective as communications with non-disabled individuals, in accordance with standards found at 28 CFR 35.130 and 35.160–35.164.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appropriate auxiliary aids and services where necessary, free of charge, in accessible formats, timely, and in ways that protect privacy and independence of the individual with a disability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of buildings and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified individual with a disability shall, because a covered entity's facilities are inaccessible or unusable, be denied benefits, excluded, or otherwise discriminated against. Facilities constructed or altered by/for a recipient or State Exchange must comply with the 2010 Standards if construction/alteration commenced on/after specified dates; departures allowed where substantially equivalent or greater access is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance tied to 2010 Standards/UFAS/1991 Standards depending on construction/alteration dates; newly constructed/altered buildings subject to 'public building or facility' definition requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of information and communication technology (ICT)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must ensure its health programs and activities provided through information and communication technology are accessible to individuals with disabilities, unless doing so would result in undue financial and administrative burdens or a fundamental alteration. If such burdens/alterations would result, the entity must take other actions to ensure, to the maximum extent possible, individuals receive the benefits/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Websites and mobile applications must comply with Section 504 as interpreted consistent with ADA Title II for recipients/State Exchanges; document undue burden/fundamental alteration analyses and alternative actions taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to make reasonable modifications (disability)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must make reasonable modifications to policies, practices, or procedures when necessary to avoid discrimination on the basis of disability, unless making the modifications would fundamentally alter the nature of the health program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret 'reasonable modifications' in a manner consistent with ADA Title II regulation at 28 CFR 35.130(b)(7); assess fundamental alteration defenses carefully and consider alternatives that provide access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal program access on the basis of sex — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must provide individuals equal access to its health programs and activities without discriminating on the basis of sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This general requirement underpins more specific prohibitions about denying/limiting services, provider participation, policies that cause more than de minimis harm, and gender-affirming care—the entity may still deny services for legitimate nondiscriminatory clinical reasons but such determinations must not be based on unlawful animus or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions regarding sex-based denial/limitation of services
rubrics_metrics.description: In providing access, a covered entity must not: (1) deny or limit services typically associated with one sex based on sex assigned at birth, gender identity, or gender otherwise recorded; (2) deny or limit a health care professional's ability to provide services if such denial/limitation effectively excludes individuals from participation or denies benefits; (3) adopt or apply policies treating individuals differently or separating them on basis of sex in ways that cause more than de minimis harm including preventing participation consistent with gender identity; or (4) deny or limit gender-affirming care provided for other purposes if the denial/limitation is based on sex assigned at birth, gender identity, or gender otherwise recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities retain ability to decline services for legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons (e.g., clinically inappropriate), but these reasons must not be pretextual or based on unlawful bias. See §§92.3 and 92.302 for protections/exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in health insurance and health-related coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must not, in providing or administering health insurance coverage or other health-related coverage, discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or any combination thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific prohibitions include denying/canceling/limiting/ refusing to issue or renew coverage, denying/limiting claims, imposing additional cost sharing or other limitations based on protected characteristics; discriminatory marketing practices or benefit designs; categorical exclusions or limitations for gender transition services; and practices that fail to provide coverage in the most integrated setting appropriate to needs of individuals with disabilities. Legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons (e.g., medical necessity) may justify a denial but must not be pretexts for discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sex discrimination related to marital/parental/family status
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether an individual satisfies any policy or criterion regarding access, a covered entity must not take an individual's sex into account in applying any rule concerning an individual's current, perceived, potential, or past marital, parental, or family status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities must avoid sex-based assumptions or rules tied to family status that have discriminatory effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination on the basis of association
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must not exclude from participation in, deny the benefits of, or otherwise discriminate against an individual or entity on the basis of the respective race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability of the individual and another person with whom the individual or entity has a relationship or association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects individuals associated with persons having protected characteristics (e.g., caregiver, family member).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in patient care decision support tools
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must not discriminate on the basis of protected characteristics through the use of patient care decision support tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities have an ongoing duty to make reasonable efforts to identify uses of decision support tools that employ input variables measuring race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability, and for each identified tool must make reasonable efforts to mitigate the risk of discrimination resulting from the tool's use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in telehealth delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must not, in delivery of its health programs and activities through telehealth services, discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telehealth modality must meet the same nondiscrimination and access obligations as in-person services, including language access, effective communication, and ICT accessibility obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The enforcement mechanisms available under title VI, title IX, section 504, and the Age Discrimination Act shall apply for purposes of section 1557 as implemented by this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1557 violations may be enforced via the enforcement tools available under these other civil-rights statutes; entities should be aware of crosscutting enforcement frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification process re: Federal religious freedom and conscience laws
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may rely on applicable Federal protections for religious freedom and conscience, and may seek assurance regarding the application of particular provisions of this part to specific contexts by submitting a written notification to the Director of OCR at any time (including before or during an investigation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification process is the mechanism for recipients to obtain assurance consistent with §92.3(c) and §92.302; submitting notification does not automatically exempt obligations absent an assurance.
